source_text: Ἰγνάτιος, ὁ καὶ Θεοφόρος, τῇ εὐλογημένῃ ἐν μεγέθει θεοῦ πατρὸς πληρώματι, τῇ προωρισμένῃ πρὸ αἰώνων εἶναι διὰ παντὸς εἰς δόξαν παράμονον ἄτρεπτον, ἡνωμένῃ καὶ ἐκλελεγμένῃ ἐν πάθει ἀληθινῷ, ἐν θελήματι τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμῶν, τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ τῇ ἀξιομακαρίστῳ, τῇ οὔσῃ ἐν Ἐφέσῳ τῆς Ἀσίας, πλεῖστα ἐν Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ καὶ ἐν ἀμώμῳ χαρᾷ χαίρειν.
thought_title: Greeting to the Church in Ephesus
orientation: Ignatius, bishop of Antioch, opens his letter to the church in Ephesus with a formal greeting while being taken under guard to Rome.
pass_a_gloss: Ignatius, the [one] also [called] God-bearer, to the [church] blessed in [the] greatness of God [the] Father [and] fullness, to the [church] predestined before [the] ages to be always unto glory abiding unchangeable, united and chosen in [the] passion true, in [the] will of the Father and [of] Jesus Christ our God, to the church most worthy of blessing, the [one] being in Ephesus of Asia, [I wish] very much in Jesus Christ and in blameless joy to rejoice.

choices.why: The name is a title meaning one who carries God; rendering it literally preserves the wordplay Ignatius uses of himself.
The term carries the sense of the complete divine presence; 'fullness' keeps the theological weight without paraphrase.
The verb means to determine beforehand; 'predestined' is the standard theological rendering and matches the perfect passive participle.
The adjective means remaining beside or enduring; 'abiding' captures the permanence of the glory.
The compound means worthy of being called blessed; the fuller rendering preserves the superlative force.
The infinitive is the standard epistolary greeting formula; rendering it as an infinitive keeps the formal Greek letter opening.

pass_b_english: Ignatius, who is also called God-Bearer, sends abundant greetings in Jesus Christ and in blameless joy to the church at Ephesus in Asia, a church most worthy of blessing. She is blessed in the greatness of God the Father in fullness, predestined before the ages to exist forever for abiding and unchangeable glory, united and chosen in true passion by the will of the Father and of Jesus Christ our God.

last_rejected.quote: by the will of the Father and of Jesus Christ our God
last_rejected.source_quote: ἐν θελήματι τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμῶν
last_rejected.why: Source has ἐν + dative ('in the will of'), not agency; English 'by' suggests means/agent, changing grammar.
last_rejected.fix: in the will of the Father and of Jesus Christ our God
last_rejected.ruling: ‘by the will’ idiomatically conveys ‘in the will’; grammar shift does not alter meaning significantly.

polish.changed: Clarified that the church is the subject of the blessings and predestination, and kept the title God-bearer consistent.

notes.why: Capitalization varies for the same title; readers may miss that it is the same designation.

problems.why: Title 'God-bearer'/'God-Bearer' vs. plural 'God-bearers' as description of believers; inconsistent capitalization.
problems.fix: Standardize capitalization and clarify when descriptive.

edits.old: Ignatius, who is also called God-bearer,
edits.new: Ignatius, who is also called God-Bearer,

fixed: The confirmed problem concerns capitalization of 'God-bearer' as a title. The English already says exactly what the source says; I standardized the capitalization to 'God-Bearer' as a title.
